mirror3: Live-action photography, not a painting. The same place as in the reference image, with the same crag of ice shaped like a frozen wave and the same towering sheet of black glass set into it, under the same burning red-orange hell sky of Avernus (never grey), but the camera has moved in close: a low-angle shot from the ice shelf at the foot of the Mirror of Mephistar, which towers forty feet high behind the figures, flawless black glass smoking with cold, and deep inside the glass the dim shape of a man in plate armour kneeling. Standing guard on the shelf, large in the frame and rendered in full detail, are five devils. Four are ice devils: each one twelve feet tall, a hulking insect-like devil built like a giant upright mantis-beetle, with a thick pale blue-white chitinous carapace rimed with frost, a broad insect head with bulging faceted eyes, antennae and heavy mandibles, powerful clawed arms, bent backward-jointed legs and a long segmented tail ending in a club of spikes; each grips a long barbed spear of black ice. Two ice devils stand in the near foreground, one at the left and one at the right of the frame, seen from the knees up and turned toward the lens; the other two stand further back, flanking the glass. Between them, at the centre before the glass, stands the bone devil lieutenant: a gaunt nine-foot devil of dry yellowed hide stretched tight over its skeleton, with a fanged skull-like face, ragged bat-like wings and a long bony scorpion tail arched over its shoulder, holding a hooked polearm. Every devil is a massive, solid, armoured creature with clear anatomy; none of them is thin and none is a stick figure. Cold blue light glows inside the ice and frost mist drifts along the ground. No humans, no soldiers, no armies.
dumal-champion: Live-action photography, not a painting. The man from the reference images, with the same face, the same short dark hair and the same dark red-and-black plate armour and tattered black cloak, walks out of the Mirror of Mephistar: behind him stands a towering sheet of flawless black glass set in a crag of ice, and its surface ripples like dark water where his trailing shoulder and cloak are still passing through it. He is a Bhaalspawn, a child of Bhaal the Lord of Murder, and it shows plainly. His eyes burn with a baleful red-gold light, like coals. On the chest of his breastplate is the symbol of Bhaal, a white human skull encircled by a ring of blood-red teardrops, glowing as if freshly branded into the steel, with dark blood running down the armour beneath it. Black-red veins crawl up his throat and along his jaw from under the gorget. Blood drips slowly from his gauntleted left hand onto the ice. In his right hand he carries the Lance of Bhaal, a long black lance with a barbed head of pale bone wreathed in cold blue-white flame, and a curved ritual dagger of carved bone hangs at his belt. In the black glass behind him his reflection is wrong: not a man, but the faint outline of a tall eyeless skull-faced monster with long claws. Frost whitens the edges of his armour and his breath smokes. The field of ice lies under the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey). Medium shot from a low angle: he fills the frame from the knees up, a handsome, careful face, calm, looking straight at the lens. No other people in the frame.
dumal-slayer: Live-action photography, not a painting. A field of black ice under the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey), and behind it, set in a crag of ice, a towering sheet of flawless black glass. In the foreground a sheet of black ice has burst open from inside, shards flying, and out of it rises the Slayer, the murder-shape of the god Bhaal: a hunched twelve-foot monster of raw red-black muscle with no skin, long limbs with too many joints, forearms ending in claws like curved blades of bone, rows of bone spines down its back, and for a head an eyeless skull with far too many long teeth, jaws gaping. The frost of Cania clings to its shoulders, forearms and spine as blue-white rime that smokes like a fresh brand. Torn shreds of dark red-and-black plate armour and a tattered black cloak still hang from its shoulders and waist, and on a cracked scrap of breastplate on its chest is the symbol of Bhaal, a white skull ringed by blood-red teardrops. Blood and meltwater run down its limbs and steam on the ice. Low-angle shot, the creature fills the frame, its head turned toward the lens. No people in the frame.
dumal-ravager: Live-action photography, not a painting. A field of ice under the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey), with a crag of ice and a towering forty-foot sheet of black glass in the background for scale. Rising over it, taller than the glass, is the Ravager: a colossal thirty-foot fiend, the murder-shape of the god Bhaal grown vast: raw red-black skinless muscle plated with ridges of black bone, long many-jointed arms ending in huge talons, a crown of jagged horns, and an eyeless skull for a head, with a maw full of long teeth and blue-white hellfire burning deep in its throat. Two enormous wings made of roaring blue-white fire are opening from its back and fill the sky behind it. The ice under its feet runs like water and freezes again as heavy iron chains, which coil up around its legs and lash through the air. In the bone of the skull, the ghost of a man's face shows for a moment, screaming. Frost and fire together: blue-white flame, black smoke, steam, embers. Very low-angle wide shot from the ice looking up, the whole creature and both wings in the frame, epic scale. No people in the frame.
cannon-broadside: Live-action photography, not a painting. The same infernal flying warship as in the reference image, the Lady Vengeance: the same long, lean galley hull of riveted black infernal iron plating, no sails and no balloon, the huge barbed harpoon launcher at her bow, cold blue-white light from the planar engine core crackling along her keel. She flies through the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey), and the camera is close off her port side and slightly below, looking along her flank. Amidships on her port rail is her port force cannon: a massive long-barrelled gun of black iron banded with brass on a heavy swivel carriage, its barrel wrapped in rings of rune-etched crystal blazing blue-white. The cannon is firing: a blinding bolt of blue-white force, a solid lance of light with a ring-shaped shockwave around the muzzle, tears away from the barrel toward a target far off-screen. The recoil shudders through the hull, arcs of lightning crawl over the plating, and heat haze and embers trail from her stern. No sails. No people visible. Epic scale, dramatic three-quarter view.
cannon-deck: Live-action photography, not a painting. On the main deck of the Lady Vengeance, the infernal flying warship from the reference image: riveted black infernal iron deck plates and rails, chains, soot and rust, with the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey) all around and the scorched wasteland and the black River Styx far below. Close shot from just behind and beside her starboard force cannon, looking along the barrel: a massive long-barrelled gun of black iron banded with brass on a heavy swivel carriage bolted to the deck at the rail, its barrel wrapped in rings of rune-etched crystal that blaze blue-white as it charges, arcs of lightning crawling between the rings, a fierce blue-white glow building in the muzzle, frost and heat haze shimmering around it. Sparks jump from the breech, where brass levers and a firing grip wait. No people in the frame: the view is the gunner's own. Shallow depth of field, the sky sharp beyond the muzzle.
film-chase: Live-action photography, not a painting. A desperate chase high in the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey), above a floor of dark ash clouds lit from below by lava. In the foreground the Lady Vengeance, the infernal flying warship from the first reference image: the same long, lean galley hull of riveted black infernal iron plating, no sails and no balloon, a huge barbed harpoon launcher at her bow, cold blue-white light from the planar engine core along her keel runs at full throttle toward the lens, her engine core blazing, a long trail of fire, embers and heat haze streaming from her stern, her black hull scorched, dented and smoking. Close behind her two dragons give chase, both clearly visible and both huge beside the ship. Behind her on the left: an adult blue dragon, the same dragon with the same face as in the second reference image: long and narrow, built like a thrown spear, scales bright azure on the back and deep indigo on the flanks, a pale belly, a single great horn on his snout capped in forged steel, banded with gold rings and filed to a point like a knight's lance, lightning running in veins through his wing membranes, a round hole the size of a shield burned clean through his left wing, static crackling over him. Behind her on the right: an adult red dragon, the same dragon with the same face as in the third reference image: bright glossy scarlet scales with glowing cracks between them like lava under a crust, heat shimmering off his back, a crown of too many swept-back horns without a chip on any of them, a spined crest down his neck flared wide, jaws open and trailing fire. Three-quarter front view from slightly below the ship, streaks of cloud and motion blur, epic scale. No sails. No people visible.
film-blue: Live-action photography, not a painting. High in the burning red-orange sky of avernus (never grey), above a floor of dark ash clouds lit from below by lava, seen from the deck rail of a flying warship of riveted black iron: an adult blue dragon, the same dragon with the same face as in the reference image: long and narrow, built like a thrown spear, scales bright azure on the back and deep indigo on the flanks, a pale belly, a single great horn on his snout capped in forged steel, banded with gold rings and filed to a point like a knight's lance, lightning running in veins through his wing membranes, a round hole the size of a shield burned clean through his left wing, static crackling over him. He banks past close alongside the ship, vast wings spread, head turned toward the lens with jaws stretched wide, and breathes a blinding straight line of blue-white lightning that rakes along the black iron deck, forks of lightning crawling over the plating and rail, sparks and molten metal flying. Low-angle shot, the dragon fills the frame, his face sharp and close. No people in the frame.
film-red: Live-action photography, not a painting. High in the burning red-orange sky of avernus (never grey), above a floor of dark ash clouds lit from below by lava, seen from the stern deck of a flying warship of riveted black iron: an adult red dragon, the same dragon with the same face as in the reference image: bright glossy scarlet scales with glowing cracks between them like lava under a crust, heat shimmering off his back, a crown of too many swept-back horns without a chip on any of them, a spined crest down his neck flared wide. He dives at the ship from behind and above, wings swept back, jaws stretched wide, and breathes a huge roaring cone of fire that washes across the black iron deck plates and the stern rail, which glow red-hot; smoke, embers and burning debris whip past the lens. Low-angle shot looking up at him, the dragon fills the frame, his face sharp and close. No people in the frame.
dumal-slayer2: Live-action photography, not a painting. A field of black ice under the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey); behind it, set in a crag of ice, a towering sheet of flawless black glass. A sheet of black ice has burst open from inside, shards still in the air, and the Slayer stands up out of it to its full height: the murder-shape of the god Bhaal. It is plainly not a man and not an undead knight. It is twice the height of a man, with a long hunched torso, arms so long the claws reach the ice, each arm with two elbows, hands like sickles of bone, backward-bent legs with an extra joint, and a ridge of long bone spines from the back of its skull down its spine. Its head is a long, narrow, eyeless skull, smooth bone where the eyes would be, with a jaw that opens far too wide and is crowded with long needle teeth. Its body is raw, wet, red-black muscle with no skin. Almost no armour is left: one cracked dark red pauldron, strips of a tattered black cloak, and one broken scrap of breastplate hanging by a strap, marked with the symbol of Bhaal, a white skull ringed by blood-red teardrops. The frost of Cania clings to its shoulders, forearms and spines as blue-white rime that smokes like a fresh brand. Blood and meltwater run down its limbs and steam on the ice. Low-angle full-body shot looking up at it, the creature fills the frame, its eyeless head tilted toward the lens. No people in the frame.
dumal-ravager2: Live-action photography, not a painting. A field of ice under the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey), with a crag of ice and a towering forty-foot sheet of black glass small in the background for scale. Towering over it stands the Ravager: the same monster as in the reference image, with the same eyeless skull head, the same raw red-black skinless muscle and the same frost on its shoulders, but grown colossal, thirty feet tall, with ridges of black bone armouring its chest and limbs, a crown of jagged horns growing from the skull, long many-jointed arms ending in huge talons, and blue-white hellfire burning deep in its throat and between its ribs. Its wings are not flesh: they are made entirely of roaring blue-white flame, two vast sheets of fire with no bones and no membrane, opening from its shoulders and filling the sky behind it. The ice under its feet runs like water and freezes again as heavy iron chains, which coil up around its legs and lash through the air. Frost and fire together: blue-white flame, black smoke, steam, embers. No armour and no breastplate. No floating faces. Very low-angle wide shot from the ice looking up, the whole creature and both wings of fire in the frame, epic scale. No people in the frame.
dumal-slayer3: Live-action photography, not a painting. A field of black ice under the burning red-orange sky of Avernus (never grey); behind it, set in a crag of ice, a towering sheet of flawless black glass. A sheet of black ice has burst open from inside, shards still in the air, and the Slayer stands up out of it: the same monster as in the reference image at an earlier, smaller stage, before it grew. It has the same horned eyeless skull head with a jaw full of long teeth and the same raw red-black skinless muscle, but it is only twelve feet tall, lean and hunched, with no wings and no fire: no blue flame anywhere, its skull dark and empty. Its arms are too long and have two elbows each, its claws are curved blades of bone, and a ridge of bone spines runs down its back. The frost of Cania clings to its shoulders, forearms and spines as blue-white rime that smokes like a fresh brand. Shreds of a tattered black cloak and one cracked dark red pauldron still hang from it, and a broken scrap of breastplate marked with the symbol of Bhaal, a white skull ringed by blood-red teardrops, hangs from a strap across its chest. Blood and meltwater run down its limbs and steam on the ice. Low-angle full-body shot looking up at it, the creature fills the frame, its eyeless head turned toward the lens. No people in the frame.
